### workspace status --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace status [options]

Show detailed state of tracked launcher sessions. Each is marked [alive] (its tmux
session exists), [dead] (the session is gone; remove it with 'workspace cleanup'),
or [unknown] (tmux didn't answer, or the project uses a custom tmux socket).

Options:
        --json                       Output as JSON
        --json-envelope              Output as JSON in the standard envelope (implies --json)

Examples:
  workspace status          # tracked sessions with window ids, headless ones marked
  workspace status --json   # machine-readable state (unique ids, window ids, alive: true/false/null)
  workspace status --json-envelope    # the same under a "status" key, with schema_version, ok and warnings
  workspace status --json | jq -r '.["my-notes"].iterm_window_id'    # one project's window id
--- stderr
--- end
